---
title: "DATA step"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r setup}
library(sasonr)
```

The DATA step is compiled into R code. Simple steps become vectorised
`dplyr` pipelines; steps with cross-row state use grouped vectorised code when
it is provably equivalent, and an explicit row loop that follows the SAS
program data vector (PDV) otherwise. Use `sas_translate()` to see the code.

This chapter is organised by topic. It grows with the DATA step
specification; every example below is part of the conformance suite.

## Conditional logic

```{r}
sas_run("
data _null_;
  do x = 1 to 3;
    if x = 1 then do; y = 'one'; z = 1; end;
    else if x = 2 then do; y = 'two'; z = 2; end;
    else do; y = 'oth'; z = 3; end;
    put x= y= z=;
  end;
run;
")$log
```

`SELECT` and the dangling `ELSE` behave as in SAS:

```{r}
sas_run("
data _null_;
  x = 5;
  select;
    when (x < 3)  g = 'L';
    when (x < 10) g = 'M';
    otherwise     g = 'H';
  end;
  if x > 1 then if x > 10 then h = 1; else h = 2;
  put g= h=;
run;
")$log
```

## Missing values

A missing numeric value is smaller than any number; arithmetic propagates
missing values, while SAS functions such as `SUM` skip them:

```{r}
sas_run("
data _null_;
  x = .;
  a = (x < 0); b = (x = .); c = (.A < .); d = (._ < .);
  e = min(x, 3); f = x + 1; g = sum(x, 1);
  put a= b= c= d= e= f= g=;
run;
")$log
```

## BY groups, RETAIN and FIRST./LAST.

```{r}
code <- "
data lab;
  input usubjid $ visit aval;
  datalines;
S01 1 10
S01 2 12
S02 1 20
S02 2 18
;
run;
data chg;
  set lab;
  by usubjid;
  retain base;
  if first.usubjid then base = aval;
  chg = aval - base;
run;
"
sas_run(code)$work$chg
```

The generated code for the second step is vectorised (level L2):

```{r}
cat(sas_translate(code)$steps[[2]]$code)
```

## LAG inside a condition

`LAG` only updates its queue when it is executed, so a conditional `LAG`
differs from a shifted column. sasonr runs such steps row by row:

```{r}
sas_run("
data a; do i = 1 to 5; output; end; run;
data _null_;
  set a;
  if mod(i, 2) = 1 then l = lag(i);
  put i= l=;
run;
")$log
```

## Arrays and DO loops

```{r}
sas_run("
data _null_;
  array a{*} x1-x3 (1 2 3);
  array t{3} _temporary_ (10 20 30);
  tot = 0;
  do i = 1 to dim(a); tot + a{i} * t{i}; end;
  s = sum(of x1-x3);
  put tot= s=;
run;
")$log
```

## Character length

The length of a character variable is set the first time the compiler sees
it, so later assignments are truncated:

```{r}
sas_run("
data _null_;
  x = 'ab'; x = 'abcd';
  if 0 then y = 'long text';
  y = 'hi';
  put x= y=;
run;
")$log
```

## Not supported yet

Features that are not verified against SAS stop the program:

```{r, error = TRUE}
sas_run("data a; x = 1; link sub; return; sub: x = 2; return; run;")
```

The DATA step specification (control flow such as `RETURN`, `LINK`,
`GOTO`, `STOP`, the execution model, multiple `SET` statements, `UPDATE`,
`MODIFY` and hash objects) is the next development focus; see
[To do and future plan](todo.html).
